overview:
Final fix round for Lucid, built from the 15 re-test reports (docs/qa/panels-r3-retest/retest.json and the .md reports) against plan.json (keep list, conflicts, deferred).

What the re-test found: most round-3 work landed (about 170 verdicts fixed, about 80 partly, 12 not-fixed). Of the 12 not-fixed, 10 are items plan.json deferred on purpose (Bagrut track, work-writing strand, speak-on-the-spot, trip phrasebook, word-order sub-types, picture vocabulary, own name in spelling, topic rotation, university genres, essay export). They are not planned again. The other two are planned: the four names for real-life situations (ux-writing-mobile), and the B1 level-check intro copy. LF-11 covers the copy, and the item bank stays deferred. All 18 major new findings are planned.

The new major findings fall into six groups:
(1) Second tries and self-credit can be gamed. The first-try note usually contains the answer: lesson.js showSecondTry shows r.retry_note/r.specific through bi(), and exercise.js ruleNote gives 'did live, not did lived' and 'the verb form the task asks for is missing: have lived'. couldBeRight lets 'went' stand for 'been' and lets 'I did live … since 2020' through. typoOnly accepts 'know' for 'known' as a spelling slip. The lesson-end note falls back to ex.explanation even when that explanation is about a different error.
(2) The lesson end and Today disagree about whether the day is done. lesson.js planLeft() uses its own done rule and settings().daily_minutes, while today.js uses planStatus with minutesToday and todayMinutes(). The 'continue the plan' key always opens #/today.
(3) Large text. At 130-150% the Settings 5-segment control overlaps itself, the lesson footer and the second-try footer take 50-59% of the screen, and the player top grows to three rows.
(4) Fairness with no sound. Listen items in lessons and in the listening hub stay answerable and scored when there is no English voice. The speaking lab handles this case, but exercise.js has no 'silent' handling.
(5) Bilingual text. Integration commit 3591997 made English align by line count (fit-content), and '.bi.he-first > .bi-he.primary + .bi-en' is text-align:right at A1. isolateLatin leaves a sentence-final full stop outside the isolate, so on a wrapped line it shows in front of the English. It also isolates comma lists and 'y: lie → lying' as one unit.
(6) Calm-mode leftovers in the games. The picture game still takes 3 points per mistake. Memory gates levels on 70% 'accuracy' and shows a slip tally. The word quiz shows a pink box saying 'לא נכון'. 'קצב רגוע' in Settings and 'אתגר מהירות' on the games hub are the same setting with opposite wording, and both are 13px native checkboxes.

Verification: I checked every planned claim in the code before planning it: planLeft and the today.js status logic; showSecondTry/selfJudge; couldBeRight/keepsVerbForm/typoOnly; mistakeNote; the focusin handler that moves the word-bank target (exercise.js:208); the speak flow skipping the verdict (lesson.js 'if (ctl.speak) next()'); learnMove saving learn_step only when a progress record exists; tableShape; .plan-item.done opacity 0.6; .bi-he-after at 0.88em; the settings .seg container query; the MISTAKE penalty and its hub copy; UNLOCK 0.7; 'לא נכון' and 'איך מנקדים?'; today.speaking set from any 'speaking' event (learner.js:414); the analyzer summary count; the evidence regex matching bare research/survey; the rebuttal regex matching 'however'; the 40-character until window; no over-regularisation rule; legend() ignoring the support level; the 'לחיים' short tab label; the reading hub with no <details>; the 7-second silent toast in app.js; the checkpoint result showing only the prompt.

Dropped claim, which I could not confirm: teacher-special-ed's 'option keycaps 1-4 visible on a touch phone' in the word quiz. app.css line 1675 hides .game-options .option .k under (hover: none) and (pointer: coarse), so this was most likely a desktop emulation without touch media features. The 'לא בדיוק' part of that finding is kept (PG-5).

Partly-fixed verdicts with no concrete remaining gap are not planned, for example the Bagrut goal 'does little' and 'more reading types', whose gaps belong to deferred content programmes. The 0.5 point for a right second try is turned down (see conflicts). Self-corrected items are labelled instead.

Lanes: 6 lanes, split by file ownership: lesson-flow, exercises, today-path, practice-games, real-life-writing and shell-bilingual. Only css/app.css and js/core/i18n.js are shared. Each lane changes only the rules and strings of its own screens, and puts new CSS in a block at the end of app.css headed '/* ---- lane r4-<key> ---- */'. A lane may edit rules elsewhere in the file only for the selectors listed in its title. No lane edits tests/e2e/run.mjs or tests/e2e/a11y.mjs. Each lane adds tests/e2e/r4-<key>.mjs and may update the existing suites it owns.

Cross-lane contracts are feature-detected, so each lane can merge alone:
(a) learner.js (today-path) exports dayStatus() and todayMinutes(). lesson.js (lesson-flow) calls dayStatus through a namespace import (`import * as learner`) as learner.dayStatus?.() and keeps planLeft() as the fallback.
(b) exercise.js (exercises) adds unheard:true to a listen result answered after silence. lesson.js (lesson-flow) and center.js runPlayer (practice-games) skip scoring when the flag is present. Without it, behaviour is unchanged.
(c) exercise.js marks a listen item's root with data-silent-inline. app.js (shell-bilingual) already tracks the play button the learner pressed. It skips the 'לא שומעים?' toast when that button has an ancestor with [data-silent-inline] (the speech event detail carries no element).
(d) The terms for real-life naming are fixed in SB-7 and recorded in docs/ux/hebrew-microcopy.md. Each lane applies them to its own files (TP-13, RW-11, PG-9).
(e) exercise.js adds short:true to a lesson writing result saved below its minimum. lesson.js colours that result amber, not green (LF-14).
(f) lesson.js logs { type: 'learn', lesson, step } when a learn step is shown (LF-6). adaptive.minutesToday (today-path, TP-2) counts the lesson's reading time when that event exists today, and keeps its current rule otherwise.

Review changes: I checked every P0 and P1 item in the code and made these changes.
(1) Wrong file or function names: LF-11's intro copy is in checkpoint.js, not player.js. RW-4's praise line is in scenario.js, and it is already hidden when an L1 issue is found, so the real gap is detection; that part of the fix is rewritten. PG-2's helper is paceOf, not paceFor. PG-12's nextSuggestion is in center.js. answerDiff is not in diff.js, so LF-2 and LF-4 now use grading.wordAccuracy and diff.js wordDiff/sentenceDiff. retrySafe moves to pool.js so that lesson.js and player.js can share it. todayMinutes is in today.js (a view), so TP-1 moves it into learner.js.
(2) Fixes that were wrong or incomplete: TP-2 relied on a 'learn' event that lesson.js does not log; contract (f) and LF-6 add it. LF-5 did not keep an unheard item out of lessonScore and missedIds, which count a missing first try as 0. LF-8 missed the cause of 'the toggle does nothing': at 130-150% the .tstack rule overrides .ipa-hidden .col-ipa. EX-6's 'Hebrew headers in parentheses' would break tableShape, which treats any Hebrew header as an RTL column and a Hebrew first header as a Hebrew table; this is now a headers_he field rendered by LF-8. The self-judge key is drawn by exercise.js verdictHtml, so LF-2 now removes it in lesson.js and guards selfJudge(). The 'did live, not did lived' note comes from exercise.js ruleNote, not from content, so EX-5 now fixes ruleNote. EX-2 is narrowed so that valid paraphrases with other verbs can still be self-credited. EX-7's amber 'short' state and EX-9's disabled-key scroll needed lesson.js; EX-7 now uses contract (e) and LF-14, and the disabled-key scroll is dropped (a disabled button gets no click). EX-11's footer button is moved into the exercise. TP-7's 'לא עכשיו' keys are already .key.ghost; the fix is now a text-button style. PG-10's .is-off fields and AI-off banner already exist; the fix is now the CSS. SB-9's clear-on-route would miss the placement result, which is a stage, not a route; the toast now ends when its play button leaves the page. Contract (c) now names the real mechanism.
(3) Keep items and conflict decisions: PG-1 no longer turns phone Settings into radio rows at 100%, which would have broken the keep item 'Settings segmented controls with one-line help text'. Only 130-150% text wraps the segments into a grid. PG-4 no longer opens memory levels above the course level for finishing boards, which broke the GM-3 decision 'above the course level, 70% accuracy'. The gate stays at 70%, measured on word-picture matches in the picture game instead of memory slips. EX-4 keeps 'transcript after answering' whenever sound works.
(4) Ownership: EX-4's listening-hub part (center.js runPlayer, practice-games) moves to a new PG-15, which also adds 'לא יודע/ת'. tutor.js's 'מצבים אמיתיים' is added to PG-9 so that SB-7's copy test can pass.
(5) Added: LF-14 (contract e) and PG-15. The memory 'ללוח קטן' link (114x31) is added to PG-4, next to the other touch-target fixes.

items.title: The lesson end agrees with Today about whether the day is done
items.problem: After a passed lesson the primary key says 'להמשיך בתוכנית: חזרה על מילים · 2 דק׳' but always links to #/today (data-plan-next). Today then says 'התוכנית להיום הושלמה' and lists the same review as optional. The cause is that lesson.js planLeft() has its own done rule (no minutesToday, no planStatus) and uses settings().daily_minutes instead of today's minutes. The end screen also says lesson.vocab.length words joined the review (9), while Today counts the cards actually added (8).
items.fix: lesson.js showReview: take the day's state from learner.dayStatus({ lesson, paces }) (contract (a) with today-path, TP-1) through `import * as learner from '../core/learner.js'`, passing this lesson's pace. Fall back to planLeft() when dayStatus is missing. When status.complete, the primary is 'סיימתם להיום · להיום' (href #/today). If a same-day first review is still undone, add a secondary 'חזרה ראשונה על המילים · לא חובה' that links straight to #/review. When the day is not complete, the primary names status.next and links to that block's own route (#/review, #/scenario/<id> …), never to #/today. Replace the vocab-count sentence with the number of cards whose source is this lesson and that were created today (allCards()).
items.acceptance: r4-lesson-flow.mjs: on a 10-minute day, finish a1-01 so that Today's minutes are met. The end-screen primary text contains 'סיימתם להיום' and its href is #/today. On #/today the done banner is present, and the word count on the end screen equals the count in Today's review row. On a 30-minute day with the review still open, the primary href is #/review.

items.title: The second try never shows the answer, and self-credit is never offered after a second try
items.problem: showSecondTry renders r.retry_note || r.specific through bi(). In 5 of the 5 cases teacher-bagrut saw, the note held the corrected form ('leave → left', 'has just passed'), and the English line repeats the Hebrew and ends with the full answer ('We eat lunch at one every day.'). exercise.js ruleNote adds 'the verb form the task asks for is missing: have lived'. After the note 'did live, not did lived', 'I did live … since 2020' gets 'גם התשובה שלי נכונה' (rendered by exercise.js verdictHtml when r.model is set), and pressing it ends the lesson at 99%.
items.fix: pool.js: add and export retrySafe(note, ex, response). It drops any language part of the note whose normalised text contains an accepted answer, or contains a key word that the response lacks (worked out with grading.wordAccuracy and diff.js wordDiff). The fallback order is the remaining part, then ex.hint, then the error-type name. lesson.js showSecondTry: pass the note through retrySafe and show only the support-language part ('he' unless hebrewSupport() is 'off'), not bi(). doCheck/showResult: when the check was a second try (wasSecond) and r.model is set, remove the '.self-judge' block from the rendered footer, and make selfJudge() return early for a second-try result. The verdict then shows the model answer as the answer. player.js uses the same retrySafe (LF-10).
items.acceptance: r4-lesson-flow.mjs: on the a1-01 'We are eat lunch…' miss, the footer after 'עוד לא. אפשר לתקן בעצמכם' does not contain 'We eat lunch' and has no lang=en element from the note at full support. On a2-05 e8, the note does not contain 'left'. On b1-02 e11, type 'I did lived in Tel Aviv since 2020.', then try again with 'I did live in Tel Aviv since 2020.': no [data-self-judge] button appears, and the answer is shown. player.test.mjs has unit tests for retrySafe.

items.title: The end-of-lesson 'כדאי לשים לב' explains the right error and shows only what changed
items.problem: pool.mistakeNote falls back to ex.explanation even when the explanation concerns a different error. For 'Have you ever went to Eilat?' the note is b1-01 e11's word-order rule. Gap items strike through and repeat a whole 25-word message for one word. An mcq choice is shown as 'wrong → right', with the flawed sentence in green as the 'correct form' (b2-09 e2). Items the learner fixed on the second try are listed as plain mistakes.
items.fix: pool.js mistakeNote(ex, response, attempt = null), keeping today's two-argument call in checkpoint.js working: use the wrong_feedback match first. Use ex.explanation only when the learner's word order equals the key's, or when attempt.error_type equals ex.error_type; otherwise return the error-type note (name_he/why_he). For gap, transform, correct and dictation items, return the pair as a word diff (diff.js wordDiff/sentenceDiff), and render only the changed words with up to 3 words of context ('we ~~plays~~ → play'). In lesson.js mistakesBox, mcq and listen items render 'בחרתם: … · התשובה: …' with no arrow and no .m-right styling. When a later attempt at the same exercise in the same run is correct after a wrong first try, the item gets the tag 'תיקנתם בעצמכם' (neutral style, check icon) instead of the struck pair. Its score is unchanged.

items.fix: lesson.js: in learnMove, and on entering learn, create the progress record when it is missing ({ id, level, status: 'started' }) before saving learn_step. Log { type: 'learn', lesson: id, step } once per step shown (contract (f) for TP-2). In showIntro, when learn_step > 0 and there is no exercise resume, the primary becomes 'להמשיך לקרוא · שלב N מתוך M' (go('learn') keeps the saved step) and the secondary is 'מההתחלה'. drawLearn shows the full title block only when learnStep === 0; later steps get a one-line title in the player top. items.title: Self-credit only when the key's verb structure is kept and agrees
items.problem: couldBeRight lets 'Have you ever went to Eilat?' through, because keepsVerbForm returns true when the key adds no verb (a pure reorder). It also passes 'I did live / I lived / I am living / I have live / I have been lived … since 2020' and 'Maya have just passed', so a wrong sentence can count as 100%.
items.fix: grading.js couldBeRight: add a check on the lexical verbs that the answer shares with the key (every verbish word of the key, not only the added ones). When the answer uses the same lexical verb as the key, it must keep the key's structure: a key participle (been, lived, known …) may not be replaced by a past or base form (went/gone for been, did + base, a bare past, have + base), and a key perfect (have/has/had + V3) may not become did + base or a simple form. Refuse these with reason 'verb'. An answer that rephrases with a different verb is left to the existing overlap rule, so valid paraphrases can still be self-credited. Add a subject-auxiliary agreement check (I/you/we/they + has, he/she/it or a singular name + have), refused with reason 'agreement'.
items.acceptance: grading.test.mjs: couldBeRight returns ok:false for 'Have you ever went to Eilat?' (key 'Have you ever been to Eilat?'); for 'I did live in Tel Aviv since 2020.', 'I lived in Tel Aviv since 2020.' and 'I have live in Tel Aviv since 2020.' (key 'I have lived in Tel Aviv since 2020.'); and for 'Maya have just passed her test.'. It returns ok:true for 'I've lived in Tel Aviv since 2020.' and for an existing passing paraphrase fixture (for example 'was held' for 'took place').

items.title: Automatic checks catch the errors Lucid's own lessons teach
items.problem: An a2-05 text with goed, eated, buyed, sleeped, 'we was', 'we see' (for the past) and 'a new shoes' got one flag ('a amazing'), though its checklist warns 'לא goed ולא buyed'. Academic texts still miss 'this tools', 'results was', 'Researches', 'The number of students increase', 'It is depend', B2 comma splices and 'Since…so'.
items.fix: writing-analyzer.js: (1) over-regularised past: an irregular base + -ed/-d from a built-in irregular list (go, eat, buy, sleep, see, take, make, come, write, think, bring, teach, catch, run, swim, begin, know, build …) → 'goed → went' (l1, from A1). (2) we/you/they/plural noun + was → were. (3) a/an + adjective + plural noun. (4) this/that + plural noun. (5) results/data/people + was, and 'the number of + plural + verb without -s'. (6) uncountable 'researches'. (7) 'it is + base verb' ('It is depend'). (8) a soft comma-splice note at B2+ (two independent clauses joined by a comma: subject-verb, comma, pronoun-verb). (9) 'Since/Because … , so'. Accept a topic option (passed by exercise.js from EX-7) and order that topic's rules first in the summary.

items.title: Argument signals do not tick on bare words, and the sweeping-word and overlap checks give fewer false alarms
items.problem: 'The research proves it.' ticks 'ראיות או דוגמאות · נמצא: research' (and 'survey' on wa-05), because the evidence regex (line 197) matches bare research/study/survey. A concession opening 'However, Merrow's strongest point…' ticks rebuttal (line 192 matches 'however' alone). 'every year', 'he learns nothing' and 'All participants completed every task.' are flagged as sweeping claims. 'on the northern edge of Orrin Fields' is flagged as copying.
items.fix: writing-analyzer.js: from stage 8, evidence needs a citation (author-year), a number or percentage, or an attributed reporting phrase (according to X, X found/showed). A bare research/study/survey becomes a soft note 'מוזכר מחקר, בלי מקור'. Rebuttal needs a counter-move after the concession (however + a contrast with the writer's own claim: 'this overlooks', 'but', 'yet'), not 'however' alone. CLAIMS skips every/all + a time noun (year, day, week, morning…), 'nothing' after a verb as its object, and sentences in a methods context ('participants', 'completed', 'were asked'). The overlap check ignores 7-grams in which at least half the words are capitalised proper nouns.
items.acceptance: writing-analyzer.test.mjs: 'The research proves it.' gives no evidence tick and one soft 'בלי מקור' note at stage 8. 'Merrow (2025) found that 40%…' ticks evidence. 'However, Merrow's strongest point is X.' with no counter does not tick rebuttal. 'every year' and 'All participants completed every task.' raise no claim issue. The Orrin Fields phrase is not flagged as overlap.

items.title: Email and own-words checks catch the work errors they promise
items.problem: In 'send you the first part, with the competitors analysis, until Wednesday', 'until' is outside the 40-character window of the until rule. 'I can't finish the report until Thursday' (meaning by) is skipped as a negative. 'Please advise' is not flagged. Own-words misses 'I am QA engineer' (a modifier before the job noun). The keyword praise in scenario.js (line 115) is already hidden when an L1 issue is found, but in the B1 stand-up 'Yesterday I finish… fix the bug until the evening' finds no issue: there is no rule for a past-time marker + present verb, and DEADLINE has no 'the evening'. So it still gets 'Your reply has words that fit this situation: yesterday'. 'I suggest to wait' and 'the app crash' are missed. Cards say 'שם עצם ספיר'.
items.fix: writing-analyzer.js: anchor the until rule on 'until + DEADLINE' anywhere in a clause containing send/finish/deliver/submit/fix (a clause runs up to . ! ? ;), and add 'the evening', 'this evening', 'the afternoon', 'today' and 'the morning' to DEADLINE. For a negative in kind 'email', add a soft note 'אם הכוונה למועד אחרון, כותבים by'. Add 'Please advise' as a soft register note. Add a past-time rule: yesterday/last <time>/<n> ago + I/we/he/she/they + a base or -s verb in the same clause → past simple (l1, from A2). Job rule: 'I am / I'm / he is / she is' + up to two modifiers + a JOB noun with no article. Add rules for 'suggest to + verb', and for 'the app/system/server + bare verb' in a past narrative. Copy: 'שם עצם שאפשר לספור (a car, a job)'. The praise logic in scenario.js stays as it is.

Rendered cards contain no 'ספיר'.

items.title: Sentence-final English keeps its own full stop, and a question mark after a single token stays Hebrew
items.problem: englishSpan leaves the full stop of an English sentence that ends the Hebrew text outside the isolate, so on a wrapped line it shows as '.I work in a bank', '.am/is/are', '.lives, watches' and '.Sorry, I'm in a bit of a hurry'. In 'זה E או I?', the '?' (which belongs to the Hebrew question) goes inside the 'I' isolate and lands mid-line.
items.fix: i18n.js englishSpan: when the run reaches the end of the string (only whitespace after it) or the next character is a line break, and the English is a sentence (two words or more, or it starts with a capital and ends with a letter), keep the final '.' inside the isolate. When the English piece is a single token of 1-3 letters (letters, symbols, IPA), leave a following '?'/'!' outside the isolate. Unit-test both against the existing BL-1 cases (list numbers, abbreviations, quotes).
items.acceptance: i18n.test.mjs: isolateLatin('… ועובדות: I work in a bank.') puts '.' inside the bdi. isolateLatin('זה E או I?') has '?' outside the last bdi. Every existing BL-1 test still passes. r4-shell-bilingual.mjs at 390/150% on the a1-01 end screen: no line in a .point visually starts with '.'.

items.title: Isolation splits English lists and prefix spans correctly, and short pairs never wrap
items.problem: In 'E ו-I, G ו-J' the run 'I, G' is one isolate, so ו- touches G, and in 's, I' the Hebrew list comma becomes English. 'הופך ל-y: lie → lying' isolates 'y: lie → lying' as one unit, displayed as 'y: lie → lying-ל'. 'lie → lying', 'make → making' and 'A = אֵיי' break across lines. 'O-M-E-' / 'R' and 'M-' / 'A-Y-A.' break at a trailing hyphen. 'Yes, I've / been there twice' splits at 30 characters.
items.fix: i18n.js: (1) In englishRuns, split a run at ', ' when every part is a single token of 3 characters or fewer (letter lists, short words), so each part is its own isolate and the comma stays Hebrew. (2) Split a run at ': ' when what follows starts a new English phrase, and keep the prefix isolate to the first token. (3) Treat 'x → y' (arrow pairs of up to 2 words on each side) and 'X = <Hebrew word>' as nw units. (4) keepSpelled also joins letter-hyphen chains that end in a hyphen or start a word ('M-A-Y-A', 'O-M-E-R'). (5) Raise NOWRAP_MAX from 20 to 30 for quotes inside Hebrew paragraphs (a unit wider than the line still wraps inside itself).
items.acceptance: i18n.test.mjs: 'E ו-I, G ו-J' gives 4 bdi elements. 'הופך ל-y: lie → lying' gives one bdi with the text 'y' and a separate one with 'lie → lying' inside a .nw. 'A = אֵיי' is inside one .nw. 'My name is Maya. M-A-Y-A.' has no breakable hyphen (U+2011 is used). r4-shell-bilingual.mjs at 390/150%: the a2-01 second-try note 'lie → lying' renders on one line.

items.title: Hebrew under English feedback is never smaller than the English
items.problem: .bi-he (0.94em) and .bi-he-after (0.88em) compound inside small text, so the Hebrew in scenario feedback computes to 11.44px, in blue on dark grey. That is smaller than the 13-15px English it translates, and it is the line an A2 learner reads.

items.title: Segmented controls never shrink below their labels, and dark mode shows the selection
items.problem: The .seg base (app.css:269) uses inline-flex with wrap and shrinkable buttons, so labels collide or wrap into ragged rows. In dark mode the selected segment (26,31,36) on the track (18,22,27) is 1.09:1 with no edge, and the active pill on the deck is 1.18:1.
items.fix: CSS .seg base: buttons get flex:1 0 auto, min-width:max-content and white-space:nowrap. When the row cannot fit, the control becomes a grid of equal cells (repeat(auto-fit, minmax(max-content, 1fr))). Dark tokens: .seg button[aria-pressed=true] gets background var(--key), a 1px var(--key-edge) border and a 2px skirt, reaching at least 3:1 against the track as a non-text indicator. Raise the deck/ground and active-pill contrast to at least 1.5:1, keeping the deck edge. The lane-owned overrides (.settings-view .seg, .ob-prefs .seg, .xp-filter-row .seg, .today-minutes > .seg) are left to their lanes.

conflicts: English alignment (BL-4): integration commit 3591997 aligned English by line count (fit-content, so a one-line instruction shares the Hebrew edge and a two-line one reads from the left), and the re-test shows two alignments in one card. plan.json's decision was 'short English titles share the Hebrew edge, and dedicated LTR content blocks are left-aligned'. Decision (SB-1): the rule follows role, not length, which keeps the original intent for titles. Titles, labels, chips and option labels share the Hebrew edge. All bi() meta-text (instructions, can-dos, hints, explanations) and all content blocks are left-aligned LTR blocks at every level. The verdict footer keeps its exception, because its keys sit on the left. BL-4d in bilingual-text.mjs is updated to the role rule.

Speed setting: Settings 'קצב רגוע' (on) and the games page's 'אתגר מהירות' (off) are one setting under two opposite names. Decision (PG-2): a single 'אתגר מהירות במשחקים' switch, off by default, shown in both places. relaxed_pace becomes derived (!game_speed_challenge). student-16 asked for auto-advance in the challenge: it is allowed for correct answers only, since plan.json's decision makes auto-advance off by default and opt-in.

Lesson end against Today: the two screens used different done rules. Decision: Today's rule (planStatus with today's minutes) is the single source, exported as learner.dayStatus() (TP-1), and the lesson end follows it (LF-1). When the day is done, an undone same-day first review is offered as an optional secondary, never as the 'continue the plan' primary.

Done minutes on Today: panels suggested freezing the minutes, counting reading time, or dropping minutes. Decision (TP-2): done blocks and the done banner show what was done (exercises, words, turns) and no minutes. The completion rule still uses minutesToday, now without double-counting replays and with reading time added through the 'learn' event (contract (f)).

Hebrew in A1 rule tables: plan.json (BL-3) kept tables English-primary as target content. teacher-adult-efl showed that a1-07's 'When?' column is the rule itself, which is meta-text. Decision (EX-6, LF-8): at Pre-A1/A1, a table's English meta column gets a Hebrew column, and Hebrew header labels go in a separate headers_he field so that tableShape's direction rule is unchanged. Examples stay English and primary, consistent with BL-3's split between meta-text and target content.

Self-credit after a second try: teacher-bagrut showed that a second-try note can lead to a wrong sentence that can be self-credited. Decision (LF-2, EX-2, EX-5): self-credit is never offered after a second try, retry notes never contain the key's words, and couldBeRight requires the key's verb structure and agreement when the answer uses the key's own verb. Paraphrases with other verbs can still be self-credited. This extends plan.json's 'second tries for typed answers only' decision; MCQ second tries stay dropped.

Memory-game unlock (PG-4) against plan.json's games decision (GM-3: levels up to the course level are open, and levels above it stay gated by 70% accuracy): teacher-special-ed and student-58 asked to unlock by finishing boards, but that would open levels above the course level with no evidence. Decision: the 70% gate stays above the course level, but in calm mode it is measured on word-picture matches in the picture game at the same level, not on memory slips. Memory accuracy counts only in the opt-in challenge. The slip tally and the '% דיוק' label are removed from calm mode.

Transcript before answering when no sound plays (EX-4) against the keep item 'transcript shown after answering': with working speech the transcript still comes after answering. With a silent device the learner can open it early, and the item is then recorded as unheard and not scored (LF-5, PG-15), so the listening evidence stays honest.

Settings segmented controls (PG-1) against the keep item 'Settings segmented controls with one-line help text': the fix keeps the segmented look and the help line, and only wraps the segments into a grid of equal cells at 130-150% text or when a row cannot fit. It does not switch to radio rows.

Scenario resume: plan.json deferred the 'Continue scenario' card on Today, and it stays deferred. RW-8 makes the saved place visible when the scenario opens and on the hub rows, in files the real-life-writing lane owns.
Score for a right second try (teacher-bagrut) against the first-try-evidence principle: no score change. The item is labelled 'תיקנתם בעצמכם' (LF-4); see deferred.

Real-life naming against plan.json's deferred 'One Hebrew form of address' sweep: this is a separate, smaller term set (four names for one thing, which the re-test marks not-fixed). It is decided in SB-7 and applied by each lane to its own files (TP-13, RW-11, PG-9). The address-form sweep stays deferred.
